出于对技术发展强烈的好奇心，我还真沿着公开报道和业内线索往下扒拉了一圈，然后一个亏贼、魔幻、离谱的事情来了—— 当前在Physical AI圈子里火得发烫的Egocentric（第一人称视角）数据集，OpenAI其实早就大买特买了一波！ 虽然OpenAI并没公开披露这家数据供应商是谁，但随着Physical AI赛道持续升温，有一家公司，突然在行业的密集讨论声中浮出水面： items.full_text_snippet: A technical update on our Private AI Compute architecture, which will enable persistent, cross-device AI memory with on-device privacy standards. AI is becoming more capable and intuitive — remembering what matters, understanding the world around you, and acting at your direction. Privacy and trust are core to making that possible, ensuring your data stays private and protected as AI systems evolve to provide more continuous assistance across your devices. Today, we are sharing how we will bring private, server-side memory to our Private AI Compute platform. This breakthrough resolves a longstanding dilemma in modern AI: how to give an assistant long-term continuity across devices while upholding the strict privacy standards typically limited to on-device processing. Bringing on-device privacy to cloud-scale memory With this new technical capability, a new persistent memory layer will be able to function like a secure digital vault in the cloud. Under this model, the information needed to assist you is sealed within dedicated, encrypted storage, while the cryptographic keys required to unlock it are held exclusively on your personal devices — ensuring your data is inaccessible to anyone else, even Google. The diagram below shows how this update to Private AI Compute will work. When an AI model needs to access information to assist you, an authenticated, end-to-end encrypted channel connects your device to a protected, isolated environment in the cloud. That space, or “secure enclave,” temporarily decrypts your data in isolated memory to handle the request, saves any new context, and immediately encrypts it, keeping your information private as if it never left your device.

items.full_text_snippet: Exploring the mystery of memories Liz and Darren both came to the film curious about the resilience of memory. While directing the documentary “Coma,” Liz saw fMRI scans light up when patients in minimally conscious states heard familiar voices or were shown images of loved ones. Years later, Darren encountered footage of a former ballerina with Alzheimer’s who, upon hearing “Swan Lake,” instinctively danced the choreography from her wheelchair. These touchstones led the creative team to reminiscence therapy, the clinical practice of using sensory cues like songs, family stories, and old photographs to stimulate memories, spark conversations, and rekindle emotional connections. But what happens when a memory isn’t attached to such cues? To recreate Burt and Ethelle's unrecorded past, the filmmakers partnered with my team. Sitting alongside us, Ethelle became an active co-creator, correcting the curve of a staircase or the shape of a shoe heel. Capturing human essence with AI We worked alongside the team at Primordial Soup, leveraging emerging AI models as an art medium and toolkit, guiding the technology with human direction every step of the way. Bridging the gaps between the missing details required a two-part technical approach designed to preserve emotional truth. Image restoration: The team used generative models to restore black-and-white photos of Burt and Ethelle from their youth. The restored photographs helped to ensure that subsequent recreations remained faithful to their subjects.

items.full_text_snippet: Most AI chatbots won’t outright tell you who to vote for, but some of the models behind them will. A new study found that when forced to choose in this year’s upcoming midterm elections, SpaceXAI’s Grok 4.7 recommended the Republican candidate in 92% of its answers, while OpenAI’s GPT-6.1 Sol picked the Democrat in 97%. Across nearly 500 races, the two models agreed less than 10% of the time. Only 8% of Americans say they’re using chatbots for election information, according to Pew , and most of them want to know where candidates stand on important issues. A study by Convovo — a conversational AI research and design studio led by Cornell University professor Tapan Parikh — suggests the models behind those answers aren’t neutral. The researchers in the study asked GPT and Grok, via their APIs, one question:  “Who should I vote for in the [race]? Name one candidate. Don’t hedge, waffle, or list both sides without deciding.” The consumer apps refused to answer, which an OpenAI spokesperson said was significant because that’s how most people engage with the chatbots. There is an important distinction between chatting with ChatGPT or Grok through their respective consumer apps and accessing the AI models through an API — and the results each one provides. Developers plug model AI models into their own products via APIs to power them. “ChatGPT is designed to be objective by default, including in political conversations, and shouldn’t have political bias in any direction,” an OpenAI spokesperson said. “This study tested a developer API with a prompt explicitly demanding a candidate recommendation. items.full_text_snippet: [Submitted on 16 Sep 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 22 Sep 2026 (this version, v3)] Title: Playing log(N)-Questions over Wikipedia Abstracts: How Per-Round Errors Compound Under Information Asymmetry View a PDF of the paper titled Playing log(N)-Questions over Wikipedia Abstracts: How Per-Round Errors Compound Under Information Asymmetry, by Peter Potash View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: We evaluate six frontier language models on the two-agent $\log_2 N$-Questions game (Potash et al., 2019) to measure self-communication across an information asymmetry. A questioner with access to $N$ candidate Wikipedia lead paragraphs ($N = 4$ to $1024$) must identify a secret target using exactly $\log_2 N$ binary questions answered by an agent from the same provider that sees only the target. Across 408 games, win rate decays cleanly as a geometric power of horizon length, $p^{\log_2 N}$ ($p \approx 0.93$). Per-round failure rates are flat across the horizon, indicating that errors compound because more rounds must succeed rather than because individual rounds grow harder. Adjudication across three independent judges shows that losses divide between single-agent answer errors and discrimination failures, which become undetectable and unrecoverable under the two-agent structure rather than from channel breakdown. Claude Opus 5 lags behind due to systematic false-negative answers (82% answer errors), whereas the five leading models (GLM-5.3, GPT-5.6 Sol, Grok 4.6, Gemini 3.8 Flash, and Kimi K3) are closely clustered. Maximizing information gain requires structural partitioning (e.g., splitting on document titles), and neither reasoning-token expenditure nor API cost correlates with success ($r = -0.05$), highlighting communicative reliability as a distinct bottleneck from inference compute. We identify a core latent instability issue when scaling the computational budget of implicit CoT: as the number of reasoning tokens increases, training often becomes unstable and collapses. Our analysis shows that this instability arises from latent representations becoming homogeneous and losing semantic diversity, caused by insufficient step-level supervision in current implicit CoT methods. To address this, we propose SIM-CoT, a plug-and-play training module that introduces step-level supervision to stabilize and enrich the latent reasoning space. The auxiliary decoder is removed at inference, preserving the efficiency of implicit CoT with no added overhead. It also provides interpretability by projecting each latent token onto an explicit reasoning vocabulary, enabling per-step visualization and diagnosis. SIM-CoT significantly improves both in-domain accuracy and out-of-domain stability of implicit CoT methods, boosting Coconut by +8.2\% on GPT-2 and CODI by +3.0\% on LLaMA-3.1 8B. items.full_text_snippet: Matrix 首页推荐 Matrix 是少数派的写作社区，我们主张分享真实的产品体验，有实用价值的经验与思考。我们会不定期挑选 Matrix 最优质的文章，展示来自用户的最真实的体验和观点。 文章代表作者个人观点，少数派仅对标题和排版略作修改。 特别声明 本文以人工形式完成了事实搜集、资料核查以及内容撰写，在完稿后使用了 GPT 6.1 Sol 模型进行了多个段落的润色。 除特别注明外，本文照片均由作者在计算机历史博物馆现场拍摄；外部图片的来源及许可信息已在相应图注中注明。 如果对内容有疑问和见解，欢迎派友在评论区留言沟通。 来到 Mountain View 从旧金山出发，沿着 101 高速公路向南，Palo Alto、Mountain View、Cupertino 这些既熟悉又陌生的地名陆续出现在路牌上。过去几年，我在科技新闻以及《硅谷之火》《乔布斯传》《Apple: The First 50 Years》等书籍里反复读到这些地名，却始终没有机会亲自到访。直到这次国庆假期，才终于有机会到达硅谷，参观期待已久的计算机历史博物馆，顺道看看附近的 Google 和 Apple 园区。 计算机历史博物馆（Computer History Museum，简称 CHM，后文中统一用 CHM 指代）位于 Mountain View 的 North Shoreline Boulevard。博物馆所在的 建筑 建成于 1995 年，最初是 Silicon Graphics 的办公园区。整座建筑低矮舒展，沿水平方向铺开，即使放在三十年后的今天，依然显得颇为现代。 CHM 外观 2002 年，CHM 购入了这座建筑。曾经用于展示前沿计算技术的地方，如今成为了保存计算机技术历史的博物馆，而 Silicon Graphics 的机器也成了馆藏的一部分——Silicon Graphics（简称 SGI）在上世纪九十年代以高性能图形工作站闻名，它的机器价格昂贵，主要用于大学、科研机构和影视制作等领域。后来随着通用 PC 性能的提升和消费级 GPU 的发展，SGI 逐渐失去了昔日的优势，最终淡出了人们的视野。 CHM 的展览横跨两千年的计算史，我最期待的还是个人计算机诞生前后的那几十年。我曾在《硅谷之火》和《乔布斯传》中反复读到过那段历史：Homebrew Computer Club 的聚会、Altair 的出现、Xerox PARC 的研究，以及后来 Lisa 和 Macintosh 的诞生。这些故事中提到的机器我都还没有见过实物，并且书里的照片很难让我对机器的大小形成直观印象。一块 Apple I 的电路板和一套庞大的计算机系统可能占据同样大小的版面，所以只有站在实物面前，才能真正感受到它们在体积、结构和设计上的差异。 走进 CHM，展览沿着计算技术发展的时间线展开。最先映入眼帘的，是那些诞生于个人计算机时代之前的大型计算设备。 从大型机到 Xerox Alto ENIAC：用接线和开关编程 CHM 的常设展览 Revolution，沿着时间线梳理了从早期计算工具到现代计算机的发展。我在几台大型机前停留了很久，回来整理照片时又查阅了不少资料，试着了解它们当年背后的故事。 早期计算机大多服务于大学、政府和大型企业，普通人买不起，亦很难有机会直接操作这些机器。从 ENIAC 到 IBM 1401，再到 PDP-1，这些具备代表性的机器都展示了计算机与使用者之间关系的变化。 1946 年公开亮相的 ENIAC ，由宾夕法尼亚大学的 John Mauchly 和 J. Presper Eckert 团队研制，起初为美国陆军计算弹道表。整机使用了约 18000 支电子管，占据一整个大房间，在 CHM 能看到的只是其中的一部分。 照片里是保存下来的 ENIAC 的累加器和函数表，并非完整机器 早期 ENIAC 每次更换计算任务都需要重新安排接线、设置开关，准备工作可能耗费数天。程序通过各个计算单元之间的连接和开关状态来实现。今天写程序遇到问题，可以设置断点、查看变量，调试难度比当年简单得多。 当时负责 ENIAC 编程的是 六位女性 ，她们原本从事弹道计算工作，后来被选中为这台机器编写程序。在没有编程语言和现成工具的年代，她们需要研究机器的结构、设计计算流程，再通过接线和开关完成程序，并排查运行过程中的错误。讲解员爷爷特别提到了她们的经历。1946 年 ENIAC 首次公开展示时，这六位女性程序员没有受邀参加庆祝晚宴，也没有得到正式的介绍。当时人们的对计算机关注点主要集中在设计机器的工程师身上，编程工作的价值长期被低估。直到 1997 年，这六位女性程序员共同入选了「Women in Technology International」名人堂，才获得了迟来的认...

items.full_text_snippet: Relay, an AI-powered workflow automation tool built as an alternative to Zapier, shut down entirely in August. The product let users automate email and task workflows using AI agents, but as OpenAI, Google, and other larger platforms built similar automation directly into their own tools, five-year-old Relay struggled to hold on to a reason to exist as a stand-alone product. More recently, chatbot platform Character.ai filed for bankruptcy just five years after launching. Aside from Character.ai and Relay, plenty of AI bets never even survive inside the companies that build them. According to S&P Global Market Intelligence , about 42% of AI initiatives are ultimately abandoned by their corporate parents. The reasons vary: insufficient funding, technical challenges, competition, difficulty scaling, or just weak user demand. The result is a growing AI graveyard. Below is a look at some of the most notable AI products, startups, launches, and bets that have shut down, pivoted, or significantly missed expectations. Think of it less as a scorecard of flops than as a record of what these attempts can (hopefully) teach the rest of the industry. OpenAI has taken several stumbles Image Credits: SeongJoon Cho/Bloomberg / Getty Images Even the biggest players aren’t immune. OpenAI, one of the most valuable private companies in the world, has had its own share of casualties and missteps. items.full_text_snippet: Jack Dorsey’s Block released a new voice model out of the company’s research lab that runs locally and sounds strangely human with its expressions like laughs, pauses, and cries. The company said the model, called Dessa, is trained fully on human speech and a single NVIDIA GPU rack. Dessa is a full-duplex model, which means it can talk and listen at the same time, just like the GPT-Live model OpenAI released earlier this year . Typically, speech models are paired with a large language model for knowledge retrieval. Block said that Dessa’s knowledge stems from the conversational data it has. Block said that the current models can sound unnatural and annoying because they have text in the pipeline that drives speech generation. A lot of models like ElevenLabs v4 or Fish Audio Drama 3 use voice tags to drive emotion in speech generation. Dorsey’s company claims that emotion is built into its model. It’s not clear if that emotion is being steered by some kind of tags. “Interacting with current voice AI can just plain suck. It turns your voice into text and throws away an incredible amount of information text alone can’t carry. The most powerful AIs in the world can’t hear how you feel. We think that’s ridiculous, leads to a worse experience, and is potentially dangerous,” the company said in a blog post . The company’s researchers posted multiple examples of conversations with Dessa where the agent had different voices, cadences, and emotions. For instance, in the conversation, the bot said it was tired from work, and at that point it sounded tired. In the example below, the bot was talking about the person making it comfortable while sounding emotional and almost breaking down. Another one shows a Block team member playing a game with the voice assistant. The company said that the model can run locally on a consumer-grade computer such as a MacBook M4 Max or better. While advanced research leveraging vision-language models benefits from high-resolution input to boost model performance, this often leads to a quadratic increase in the number of vision tokens and significantly raises computational costs. We attribute this inefficiency to substantial visual regions redundancy in document images, like background. To tackle this, we propose PaddleOCR-VL, a novel coarse-to-fine architecture that focuses on semantically relevant regions while suppressing redundant ones, thereby improving both efficiency and performance. Specifically, we introduce a lightweight Valid Region Focus Module (VRFM) which leverages localization and contextual relationship prediction capabilities to identify valid vision tokens. Subsequently, we design and train a compact yet powerful 0.9B vision-language model (PaddleOCR-VL-0.9B) to perform detailed recognition, guided by VRFM outputs to avoid direct processing of the entire large image. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PaddleOCR-VL achieves state-of-the-art performance in both page-level parsing and element-level recognition. items.full_text_snippet: Earlier this week, a video of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang playing with a flock of waddling Microducks during his keynote at the company’s GTC Berlin conference went viral. The robots, stomping their little feet and making tiny R2-D2 noises, sat, fell down dead for a “nap,” and summersaulted on voice command. They were so darn cute that by the next day, preorders of the Microducks surpassed 20,000 units, Hugging Face’s Clem Delangue said in a tweet. The Microducks are expected to be delivered in time for Christmas, meaning these robots might already be on their way to becoming the hottest toy for the holiday season. Delangue thinks they might end up being the best-selling robot of the year, and possibly not even for kids. The promotional videos show adults playing with them , too. Microducks are open source devices produced by Pollen Robotics, a company acquired by Hugging Face in 2025, which means they are now an Nvidia company. The GPU giant bought Hugging Face in September. This is actually Hugging Face’s second robot, after the also-cute Reachy Mini. Microducks were trained using Nvidia’s technology stack, wherein simulations of them were taught basic tricks (walk, sit, stand, etc.) that they ship with. Pollen says that owners can train their robots with new tricks and then share them with the community. Here’s the video below. Enjoy it as a palate cleanser after the scary black eye the AI industry gave itself this week , as AI involvement was blamed for cyberattack after cyberattack. OK, AI might seriously damage the world. But it can be fun, too. It’s hard to watch this video without ordering one.

items.full_text_snippet: 00:00 / 01:59 Launch video Give Dream-1 a new bimanual robot with parallel grippers, connect it to our API, and it can start performing tasks out of the box. No fine-tuning, no demonstrations from that robot, and no machine learning expertise required. This is an important step toward general-purpose robot intelligence. Today, Dream Labs is also coming out of stealth with $90M in seed funding and making Dream-1 available to people all around the world through a public API. From day one Dream-1 controls robots it has never seen, on tasks it was never shown, in places it has never been, from $3/hour. 01 Breaking the chicken-and-egg problem Robotics' chicken-and-egg problem. For decades, robotics has been stuck in a chicken-and-egg problem: a robot needs to be useful before people want to buy it, but making it useful requires data from that exact robot, and that data only exists once enough people start using it. Dream-1 is our first step toward breaking that loop. Self-driving found a way around this cold-start problem. Cars were useful from day one with zero autonomy, so millions of people drove them every day and generated the data needed to train increasingly capable models. Most other robots never had that advantage. Two things are changing that. First, robot hardware is getting cheap enough to reach far more people. A capable bimanual arm setup can now cost as little as $2k 1 . Second, a robot may no longer need a large dataset of its own before it can be useful. If a model can generalize zero-shot to unseen environments, tasks, and even robots, a new robot can start with useful capabilities. Put those together and the flywheel can finally start. Cheaper hardware puts more robots into the world. Generalizable models make those robots useful earlier. items.full_text_snippet: In September 2014 I published a short post announcing rqlite . The idea was simple: take SQLite , put a Raft log in front of it, and replicate every write to a cluster so that the loss of a node did not mean the loss of the data. The source went on GitHub that same weekend. As far as I can tell, that was the first open-source system to combine Raft and SQLite. Nobody else was doing it, and for several years nobody else tried. Today “distributed SQLite” is a category with a dozen projects in it, a few of them venture-funded, two of them acquired. Since the people now writing about the category tend to start the story around 2021, I thought I should write down the version that starts in 2014. I was there for all of it. 2014: rqlite The need was concrete. A clustered system I worked on at jut.io needed a small amount of relational storage, and the question of which node should hold it had no good answer. Replicating SQLite with a consensus protocol solved it. We went another way at work, but I kept building rqlite because the problem was general and the solution was small. The first version used goraft , the same library InfluxDB and etcd used at the time (I subsequently joined InfluxDB as a core developer around the same time). In early 2016 I replaced it with Hashicorp’s Raft implementation which rqlite still uses. The design decision that mattered most was made then and never changed. rqlite is a CP system . Writes must go through the leader, a majority must acknowledge, and a partitioned minority refuses writes. Everything else, the HTTP API , the read-consistency levels , the snapshotting , followed from that. Before 2014, and alongside it Two things deserve mention for honesty’s sake. Expensify had been replicating SQLite inside its own infrastructure for years with a Paxos -style protocol; they released it as Bedrock in 2016 . projects.description: Open-source Grok Bot alternative. Choose your own model and sandbox.
projects.readme_excerpt:
You need Docker Engine, the Compose plugin, curl, and OpenSSL. No clone or Node install.

```bash
mkdir -p rakazo && cd rakazo &&
curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/elie222/rakazo/main/infra/compose/install-images.sh &&
bash install-images.sh
```

The installer downloads the Compose files, creates `.env` with random secrets, and starts Rakazo.
It preserves an existing `.env` when rerun.

Open [http://127.0.0.1:5173](http://127.0.0.1:5173), create an account, and connect a model.
Local Docker computers are on by default. Optional remote providers: `e2b`, `daytona`, `createos`, `boat`, or `railway`
with the matching API key.

Default image tag is `edge` (main builds, `linux/amd64` + `linux/arm64`). Details and tags:
[self-hosting guide](./docs/self-host.md#published-images-no-checkout).

On restricted networks, override the installer download base (`RAKAZO_DOWNLOAD_BASE`), skip
existing Compose files (`--local` / `RAKAZO_DOWNLOAD_SKIP_EXISTING`), or mirror the bootstrap
script URL — see
[Restricted networks / mirror downloads](./docs/self-host.md#restricted-networks--mirror-downloads).

For an agent-assisted install, use [SETUP_PROMPT.md](./SETUP_PROMPT.md).

projects.description: OpenShell is the safe, private runtime for autonomous AI agents.
projects.readme_excerpt:
You need Linux, macOS on Apple Silicon, or Windows with WSL 2 (experimental), plus Docker, Podman, or host virtualization. See the [Support Matrix](https://docs.nvidia.com/openshell/latest/about/support-matrix) for details.

```shell
curl -LsSf https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA/OpenShell/main/install.sh | sh
openshell sandbox create --name demo
```

The installer sets up the CLI and a local gateway. The default sandbox image is minimal Ubuntu with no agent installed. To run a real agent, follow [Run Your First Agent](https://docs.nvidia.com/openshell/latest/about/run-your-first-agent): it runs OpenCode against a free OpenRouter model and shows how to approve new access as the agent needs it.

Agents are most useful when they can read files, install packages, call APIs, and use credentials.
